_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how many matched translation units actually reach the
PC port's binary. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
This number moves ONE way: seating a new actor class, worth ~8-10 TUs each.
Enrolling free TUs does nothing, because the release build dead-strips whatever the
linked closure never references.
basis: integration branch port/link100 at its pushed tip 4e7df8daf, measured against that tip's own battery build walk_window.map (C:/tmp/l1-int, gate INT10: tree clean, battery ALL GREEN at floor 10044, six proofs green including the opening-cutscene gate), and confirmed by the hosted-runner port-linkage workflow, which now counts every push of port/** and the shipping branch on a GitHub Windows machine with no cartridge and printed the same number for the previous two pushes. +25 over the 2026-09-08 morning stamp of 10033 and +937 over the 2026-08-30 stamp of 9121. The shipping branch port-mount-noseat-cluster is fast-forwarded to the same commit. Since the 10033 stamp: eleven calling-convention host copies retired on ROM words read at their own addresses (daDoor_c::Render on Model slots 4 and 5, the Goomboss, ShipUp and FloatOnWaterPlatformJrb Renders, four ov006 MgD3DBase bodies reached by arm calls, the Platform base, Player::BlowAway), the thirteen free pointer-to-member dispatchers plus Bird::Behavior (fourteen), with a record-stride defect found and fixed first: MSVC aligns a struct containing a pointer-to-member to eight, so the ROM's twenty-byte state records were being indexed at twenty-four and eleven of the thirteen tables would have dispatched wrong from state 1 on; a per-source /Zp4 restores the ROM's stride. Tooling in the same span: the alias guard rewritten (the 76 directives in vs_aliases.inc are measured, commented-out pragmas are prose, thumb-masked address agreement over 1666 rows), the boot-pair proof rung fixed, and the port build no longer reconfigures on every build (238 configure-time inputs registered). Gated rungs since the last stamp: 10033 -> 10044 -> 10058. Remaining: the 120 call-shape rows of the pointer-to-member family (a __fastcall face each, the seats first), the dScMgBase framework installer, the wireless chain behind the ARM7 model (~175), the boot chain's refused arms, and guessed vtable bodies that need real decomp.
